Data and interpretation

Each paper was assessed in a fresh GPT-5.6 Sol session at medium reasoning effort, using the shared prompt and published main article. The analysis uses archived model outputs and retains their original scores.

  • Unit: one experiment–criterion assessment. All applicable components must be met for a criterion score of 1. N/A is excluded from the denominator.
  • Weighting: every applicable experiment contributes one observation per criterion. Papers containing more experiments contribute more observations. Domain summaries pool the applicable criterion assessments in that domain.
  • Experiment roles: classes 1–3 correspond to primary, supporting and diagnostic experiments. Classes 4–5 remain available in the full paper inventories.
  • Review: human methodological review is pending. Structural checks cover output fields and source references. The check filter supports a descriptive comparison using records that pass those checks.
  • Comparisons: journal summaries describe these collections and their mix of experiments. Role filters support comparisons within the same experimental role. Missing-detail counts reflect the model's reporting judgments.
